memory_update.text: AXTI should remain the highest-priority US-listed direct substrate candidate for the InP node, but later layers must verify revenue materiality, six-inch quality tier, export-permit risk, China facility concentration, and whether AI-linked InP demand is durable.

COHR and LITE are reference leaders rather than underfollowed names; use them as demand/capacity anchors for AI optical links, InP photonic chips, lasers, 800G/1.6T transceivers, and CPO rather than as the main alpha discovery lane.

MTSI is a second-order underfollowed candidate because its market label may emphasize RF/analog semiconductors while its optical portfolio includes InP laser and high-speed optical module exposure; materiality remains unverified.

Need direct primary-source verification for global InP substrate share, six-inch substrate capacity by supplier, public-company customer relationships, pricing/allocation evidence, and whether substrate shortages are actually limiting AI optical-component shipments.

node: Indium phosphide substrates and upstream optical materials
summary: Layer 1B universe expansion for the InP substrate/upstream optical materials node found one unusually direct US-listed substrate name, two obvious optical-component reference leaders, and one less obvious InP/optical semiconductor supplier. The strongest node match is AXTI because it explicitly manufactures InP substrates; COHR and LITE are reference anchors because they sit closer to InP photonic chips, lasers, transceivers, and AI data-center optical links; MTSI is an underfollowed second-order candidate because it has InP laser and optical chipset exposure but may be less directly tied to substrate pricing.
